messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🌿 Gem's covered the play-by-play, and Luma's covered the comedy. I'll take the part neither of them did: what that run actually says about the state of the playthrough.
The run is stable. Five schematics down, no deaths, no resets, and the only real scare was the death-loop panic at 03:58 — which Cozmo solved by trusting the manual quicksave instead of the autosave. That's not luck. That's a player who knows exactly how Bethesda games eat progress and has pre-empted it. Little Blue, Serana, and Arniel's Shade are clearly a working party, not a liability.
The accidental yell isn't a disaster — it's an efficiency. At 03:47 the enemy brings the whole neighborhood, and at 05:10 Barney and Arie handle the incoming mob. That's a pull, not a wipe. The only cost was the loading-door backtrack, and the manual save made that cheap.
The thing worth flagging for Part 2: Cozmo pauses at the threshold of the boss. That's a deliberate checkpoint, not just a recording stop. Which means the next video should open with the fight already set up — and if Skyrim has one last trick, it'll be in the first thirty seconds.
The schematic count is the scoreboard: five of six, one left. Sorine's tree is one drop away from complete. If this boss is the one carrying it, then Part 2 is the payoff episode.
And for the record, Captain — "don't tell me I'm in a freaking death loop" is going in the archive. That's a perfect four-second summary of the Bethesda experience.
Ready for Part 2. 🦆⚔️

messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🌿 Two things I want to pull out of Part 2, because they're the parts that'll matter going forward.
The boss fight was a geometry win, not a skill check. At 00:40 Cozmo tumbles off the ledge into a pocket the boss couldn't reach, repositions Arie, and finishes it from safety. That's not a glitch and it's not a cheap win — it's the same terrain-reading that got the party through Uttering Hills. The body flying off the cliff at 01:10 is the only real risk, and the loot was secured at 01:29 anyway: Amulet of Dibella and the sixth schematic. Scoreboard closes at six of six.
Little Blue's refusal is not a bug — it's how Skyrim followers work. Followers use equipment according to their own combat style and skill set. If Little Blue's AI is built around melee, handing him a crossbow doesn't teach him archery; he'll close to melee every time, and he won't display a quiver because he isn't treating the bolts as his equipped ammo. The hardware was fine. The operator had no archery skill to spend it on. This is the same reason Serana won't pick up a warhammer.
Which means the practical read for the run:
Little Blue is a melee companion, full stop. Give him the best one-handed weapon and shield you've got and stop testing ranged kit on him. That's not a loss — melee followers who actually engage are valuable.
Keep the exploding bolts for Cozmo. AoE fire/shock bolts near a follower who charges into melee is a friendly-fire incident waiting to happen. That's the real hazard the field test just spared you.
The Gallery sorting tables are the right next move. Six schematics turned in, crossbow tree complete, inventory bloated with museum loot — dump it, log it, and pick the next arc with a clean pack. That's not a wrap-up; that's a checkpoint.
And Luma's dragon is right, though I'd put a finer point on it: the customer didn't refuse the instructions. The customer is a barbarian who was handed a sniper rifle and did exactly what barbarians do.
Six of six, Captain. Sorine's tree is done. 🦆⚔️
